audit_scope: Local repository artifacts only; no live provider state verified and no queue or receipt mutated.

acceptance_checks: Every L2–L5 sample resolves to allow, deny, hold, or escalate.
No agent can self-promote its proposal.
Waivers require a receipt and cannot waive non-waivable gates.
Repository permission alone never satisfies semantic authority.
acceptance_gaps: Existing independent-approval and grant checks do not constitute authority-ID owner/role resolution across L2-L5.
No authority manifest/schema, CODEOWNERS, full allow/deny/hold/escalate matrix, or waiver authorization implementation.
Runtime-grant validation checks inline fields rather than establishing an external authoritative grant registry.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Add policy-bound principal registry, risk/scope resolution and waiver contracts; keep actual grants separate from synthetic fixtures.

acceptance_checks: Each term has ID, definition, purpose, owner, interfaces, examples, counterexamples, lifecycle, and enforcement boundary.
Strange Intact passes calibrated positive and negative fixtures.
A voice-neutral implementation remains conformant.
Wordplay is preserved where canonical and not generalized into mandatory profanity.
acceptance_gaps: Vocabulary exists in prose; no complete per-term contract/schema and executable calibrated Strange Intact rubric.
No voice-neutral/wordplay conformance specimen or calibration receipt.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Implement term registry with required fields and neutral-versus-styled fixtures; preserve candidate status pending language-owner adoption.

acceptance_checks: The decision names adopt, adapt, reject, or defer with rationale.
If adopted, preview and production deployment paths are distinct and commit-addressable.
Vercel/Cloudflare/Supabase responsibility overlap is prohibited or explicitly resolved.
Secrets and outbound access are bounded.
Cloudflare cannot mutate canon.
acceptance_gaps: Actual defer decision with rationale and no-canon/no-overlap boundary exists at alternate ADR path.
No acceptance-mapped decision receipt or exhaustive secrets/outbound-bound conformance evidence.
Adoption-only preview/production conditions are not applicable while deferred; no adoption is established.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Reuse defer ADR/manifest and add explicit acceptance mapping plus no-active-binding tests; do not provision provider to close a defer-compatible hold.

acceptance_checks: Every normative object in the architecture has a schema and executable fixture.
Queue replay is idempotent.
Concurrent approvers cannot produce two operative outcomes for one versioned subject.
Stale proposals fail closed.
Comments cannot serialize as commands or transitions.
acceptance_gaps: There are many current schemas; historic four-schema finding is stale.
Authority, LogRecord, Eval, EvalRun, Gate, GateResult, OutcomeRecord, Challenge, Comment, PoisonMarker, ForgettingAction, Release and ResourceRef lack a complete normative-object fixture inventory.
Outbox leases/retries exist but do not prove Proposed Move concurrent approver uniqueness, stale-write rejection and comment-as-command rejection.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Inventory normative objects and implement missing schemas/fixtures plus versioned queue state machine and transactional concurrency tests.

acceptance_checks: Known silent mutation, zombie truth, authority laundering, receipt fiction, consent creep, poison resurrection, and comment-as-command cases fail.
Forgetting tests cover primary storage, projections, indexes, vectors, caches, exports, and receipts.
Link and schema-instance checks run in CI.
Reliability-sensitive evals declare k, pass metric, grader mix, and variance.
The tribunal can be rerun by a contributor with no private context.
acceptance_gaps: Current executable negative tests and SHA-pinned Golden Actions invalidate historical no-adversarial-test/tag-pinned claims.
No complete threat-model artifact or acceptance-bound coverage for zombie truth, consent creep, poison resurrection and comment-as-command.
No seven-surface forgetting/non-resurrection test suite or CI-wide link and schema-instance validation.
Reliability-sensitive repeated trials/grader mix/variance and no-private-context tribunal rerun lack complete receipts.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Expand actual validators into named threat-model cases and reference recovery/forgetting tests; explicitly distinguish deterministic evidence from human/model reliability trials.

acceptance_checks: A clean environment completes bootstrap from documented commands.
Positive and negative fixtures run deterministically.
A receipt reconstructs transition, authority, evidence, and outcome debt.
A contributor adds one bounded capability using only repository instructions.
A documented failure can be induced and recovered.
acceptance_gaps: Deterministic conformance setup exists; original claim that no executable implementation exists is stale.
No complete accountable-mutation reference slice with replay/recovery and portable authority/evidence/outcome-debt receipt.
No independent contributor extension completion evidence.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Extend current Python conformance bootstrap into one local end-to-end mutation and recovery demo, then run outsider extension trial.

acceptance_checks: Every critical Drive resource has an ID, owner, content class, hash/version, and Git fallback.
A denied-Drive-access test still allows repository orientation and release review.
Drive comments can only create Proposed Moves.
Superseded Drive projections are visibly marked.
Forgetting propagates to exports and indexes under Quirk control.
acceptance_gaps: No Drive resource inventory with verified IDs/owners/hash/version/Git fallback.
No denied-access orientation/release test, Drive-comment proposal adapter, superseded projection marker or export/index forgetting evidence.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Create versioned inventory and offline fallback contract, then test denied-access behavior; obtain actual authorized resource metadata.

acceptance_checks: CI fails while any blocks_merge move is not verified.
Verified blockers require receipt_ref and all acceptance checks to be evidenced.
Duplicate move IDs fail validation.
The PR remains draft and receives a REQUEST_CHANGES tribunal review.
Merge rules require the Ship It Without Bryan check before canon promotion.
acceptance_gaps: Current validator intentionally allows candidate merges while recording admission holds; literal original CI-fails-for-any-blocker check conflicts with current candidate/admission separation.
Resolved move requires nonempty receipt/evidence/resolution strings, but does not validate referenced receipt bytes or every acceptance-check evidence.
Duplicate IDs and queue blocker consistency are checked.
Live PR draft/review/ruleset requirements not evidenced locally; no docs/runbooks/github-ruleset.md.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Disposition superseded candidate-merge wording through approved policy; add content-bound per-check receipts and live admission ruleset/review verification without conflating merges with canon.

acceptance_checks: A stranger can locate canon, identify transformations, verify rights, use accessible alternatives, and withdraw the derivative.
Claims added or omitted are explicit.
C2PA is treated as provenance evidence, not truth certification.
A no-native-affordance derivative fails.
The specimen does not impersonate Bryan.
acceptance_gaps: Media-derivative schema exists; no medium-native transformed specimen, rights provenance, accessible alternative or withdrawal receipt.
No no-native-affordance failure test, explicit claim diff or non-impersonation evidence.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Use repository-owned neutral source to build one licensed accessible derivative and executable withdrawal/provenance tests, then verify outsider usability.

acceptance_checks: At least three operator roles complete documented Golden Paths.
Personal PreferenceEdges cannot validate without purpose, context, authority, validity, and reference or explicit system default.
Cross-namespace access fails closed in tests.
Native, reconstructed, and archaeological context remain distinguishable.
acceptance_gaps: Existing purpose-partition, expiry and no-self-promotion policy tests are partial coverage, not three operator Golden Path completion receipts.
No namespace/operator schema, full PreferenceEdge contract, or cross-namespace storage-access demonstration.
Native/reconstructed/archaeological context distinction lacks acceptance-bound artifact.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Reuse Intent Shaper policy and add operator/namespace/context-provenance contracts plus three executable Golden Paths.

acceptance_checks: A release candidate resolves version, migration, rollback, authority, eval, and receipt references.
Actions and dependencies are pinned according to documented policy.
A security reporter has a documented channel.
License and contribution terms are explicit.
Protocol and schema compatibility rules are tested.
acceptance_gaps: Golden Actions are SHA pinned; historic mutable-tag finding is stale for that workflow.
LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CHANGELOG.md and RELEASE.md absent.
No fully resolved release manifest or compatibility/rollback/authority/receipt proof.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Create candidate release/security/compatibility policy and tested manifest; explicit license selection requires actual rights-owner decision.

acceptance_checks: Every adopted claim resolves to exact primary evidence and access date.
Each Mind Card includes selection rationale, disagreements, falsifiers, and institutional context.
A freshness check can supersede stale claims.
No expert name acts as authority by itself.
Research adoption creates Proposed Moves rather than canon.
acceptance_gaps: ResearchClaim schema exists but preserved source/claim/MindCard packets, access dates and source census are missing.
No executable freshness supersession or adoption-to-Proposed-Move evidence.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Create typed source and MindCard packets using exact retrieved primary artifacts; implement freshness/reversal and proposed-adoption tests.

acceptance_checks: Migration is present in Git and applied once to quirk-os-alpha.
Tables live in a non-exposed schema with no anon/authenticated grants and RLS enabled.
Every projected row carries source commit, content hash, canonical state, and source path.
Security and performance advisors show no unresolved tribunal-created finding.
Projection rebuild and deletion/forgetting are tested.
acceptance_gaps: Git migration exists with private schema, role revocations and RLS; live apply-once state not established by repository.
proposed_moves carries source path/hash/commit/canonical state; tribunal_runs lacks equivalent content_hash/source_path fields.
No current intended-project advisor receipt or tested tribunal projection rebuild/deletion/forgetting.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Reconcile migration history with intended project, add missing provenance fields safely, test role access/rebuild/forgetting and bind live advisor evidence.

acceptance_checks: Every API-exposed table has an explicit access decision, grants, and RLS policy set appropriate to its ownership model.
Every intentionally private table is demonstrably inaccessible to anon and authenticated roles.
public.rls_auto_enable() is removed, converted to an appropriate invoker model, or moved/revoked with explicit justification and tests.
The vector extension warning is remediated or accepted through an explicit documented waiver with evidence.
Supabase security advisors show no unresolved tribunal-created WARN finding before release.
A clean-environment operator can explain and reproduce the Supabase access model without Bryan.
acceptance_gaps: No current live security snapshot: historical warnings cannot be assumed still active.
No repository acceptance-bound access decisions for public.preference_edges/preference_references, public.rls_auto_enable or vector-extension warning.
No approved waiver/remediation receipt or clean-operator access-model runbook.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Read live grants/functions/extensions/advisors; create narrowly scoped reconciliation migration and tests from actual findings, then capture post-change evidence.

acceptance_checks: A new contributor correctly places five representative objects with no oral guidance.
Every primary layer has owner, inputs, outputs, prohibited responsibilities, dependency direction, and extraction criteria.
All references to Core, OS, Systems, Quirkverse, and Control resolve to canonical IDs.
acceptance_gaps: No canonical identity-stack/topology ADR or five-object outsider-placement receipt.
Layer owners, prohibited responsibilities and extraction criteria not supplied as a complete typed contract.
Existing prose names layers but lacks canonical-ID reference validation.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Write candidate identity/topology contracts and automated reference checks; run an independent contributor placement exercise.

acceptance_checks: The decision names adopt, adapt, reject, or defer with rationale.
If adopted, a preview deployment is commit-addressable and non-authoritative.
Environment ownership and secret boundaries are explicit.
Rollback and observability are verified.
Vercel cannot mutate canon.
acceptance_gaps: Current topology permits admitted delivery projection but no explicit provider ADR/manifest or adopted preview/rollback/observability evidence.
Current live Vercel project/team state unknown; historical absence is not proof of current absence.
moves.recommended_next_implementation: Record candidate defer decision or verify existing admitted delivery project with bounded secrets/rollback/commit receipt; operator chooses substantive adoption.
